Plant Nutrients - Essentially all overburden and interburden materials had very low concentrations of nitrate and ammonia nitrogen. The status of potassium, calcium, magnesium and sulfur was adequate to sample for plant growth based on analysis of material from about 40 percent of the drill holes on Tract III. Phosphorus was deficient throughout the overburden and interburden.
Plant micronutrients include zinc, iron, copper, manganese, boron and molybdenum. In general, micronutrients were present in suitable concentrations for plant growth and intervals where uptake of one micronutrient might be inhibited by excessive concentrations of another were rare. Intervals deficient in one or more micronutrients were common.
Zinc levels (determined by DTPA extraction) normally did not exceed 40 ppm, but concentrations as high as 448 ppm were encountered sporadically. Such occurrence suggests a contamination problem, and Westmoreland Resources has found that the compound used to join the drill pipe was 50 percent zinc. Although it is unlikely that zinc concentrations in the ranges observed would be phytotoxic, overburden mixing should dilute high zinc intervals such that in most cases zinc levels in spoil material probably will be comparable to levels normally encountered in surface soils.
